label: Rail vehicle
description: Locomotives, passenger and freight trains, urban rail, individual railcars, and small work vehicles.
frame: a view of the ___ on the tracks
notes: Rail vehicles belong here, covering complete trains, locomotives, distinctive passenger and freight cars, and small work vehicles. vehicle.road_vehicle owns road traffic, including buses; street-running trams remain here because they follow rails. Values are bare type names without operators, manufacturers, routes, or liveries. Heritage and contemporary equipment share the list, and tram and streetcar entries distinguish articulated low-floor and traditional single-car forms.

values.look: A rail engine with a cylindrical boiler, smokestack, large driving wheels, and exposed connecting rods.
A long boxy engine with a raised cab, side walkways, and large grilles along its hood.
A boxy rail engine with roof-mounted pantographs reaching up to overhead power wires.
A sleek passenger train with an elongated pointed nose and smoothly connected cars.
A smooth streamlined train wraps around a raised guideway without visible conventional wheels.
A line of short metal passenger cars with frequent wide sliding doors and flat cab ends.
A long street-running rail vehicle with several flexible joints, broad windows, and doors near pavement level.
A short single railcar with a rounded roof, tall windows, wood trim, and a roof-mounted trolley pole.
A compact street railcar with open running boards, wooden benches, and enclosed central seating.
A short passenger car with a stepped body on a steep hillside track, pulled by a cable.
An elevated passenger train rides on one thick beam rather than a pair of rails.
A locomotive hauls a long mixed line of boxcars, tank cars, and other cargo wagons.
A long passenger railcar with a corridor-side window row and separate sleeping-compartment windows.
A passenger railcar has a raised glass observation dome extending above the main roof.
A passenger train has two stacked rows of windows and tall cars between lower vestibules.
A compact mountain train climbs steep rails above a visible central toothed rack.
A small steam engine has a tilted boiler and exposed geared drive for a steep mountain railway.
Passenger cars hang below a single overhead rail, with wheels and supports above the roof.
An enclosed rectangular freight car with a corrugated metal body and a large sliding side door.
A horizontal cylindrical tank sits on a rail underframe with a small top loading dome.
An open-topped freight car has sloping lower walls and funnel-shaped unloading bays beneath.
A low flat rail platform with exposed cargo tie-downs and no enclosed sides or roof.
A small open metal ore tub sits on four tiny flanged wheels.
A small open rail platform has a central seesaw pump handle used to drive its wheels.
A heavy rail vehicle has a huge circular rotary blade inside a broad front housing.
